SESSION_TURN_SETTLED.definition: session.status is not one of UNSETTLED_SESSION_STATUSES (PENDING, RUNNING).
isNot: SESSION_RUN_TERMINAL: AWAITING_INPUT and INTERRUPTED are settled but not terminal.
TASK_DONE: a settled turn says nothing about the task's completion criterion.

SESSION_RUN_TERMINAL.definition: deriveSessionRunState is one of SUCCEEDED, FAILED, ENDED.

SESSION_LIFECYCLE_TERMINAL.definition: deriveSessionLifecycleState is one of COMPLETED, TRASH.

SESSION_NEEDS_ATTENTION.definition: At least one Approval row for the session has status PENDING.

TASK_TERMINAL.definition: task.status is one of DONE, CANCELLED, FAILED.

TASK_DONE.definition: task.status is DONE, which is the projection of a satisfied completion criterion and never a direct write.

RESUME_SESSION only: the observer's run ended while the wake turn was still queued (a Match's, keyed watch:<watchId>:<generation>, or a watch end's, keyed watch:<watchId>:expired, :revoked or :unresolvable), and the drain that ended its queue answered the wake before any runner took it (OBSERVER_SESSION_ENDED)

RESUME_SESSION only: the observer was interrupted while the wake turn was still queued, and the interrupt deleted the wake with every follow-up queued behind the turn it stopped, before any runner took it (OBSERVER_TURN_INTERRUPTED)
RESUME_SESSION only: the owner withdrew the queued wake turn before any runner took it, and the withdrawal deleted that turn alone (WAKE_WITHDRAWN)

delivery.deliveredNote: DELIVERED is final for NOTIFY_USER and for a wake a runner has taken. A RESUME_SESSION delivery, a Match's or a watch end's (EXPIRED, REVOKED or UNRESOLVABLE), is DELIVERED once its turn is queued; until a runner takes that turn, three things take the wake off the queue and make the delivery a dead letter: the end of the observer's run drains it, an interrupt of the observer deletes it with the rest of the queue, and the owner withdrawing it deletes that one turn. None of them is redelivered. A wake never revives an ended session, and a drained turn cannot be delivered again under its key; an interrupt means stop, so a wake kept queued or redelivered would wake the observer right after it was stopped; a withdrawal is the owner taking the wake back.

match.note: A Match is a fact about the world. It is not a notification; the effect is a WatchDelivery.

actions.effect: One user-visible notification, counted by the existing needs-you badge path.
Enqueue exactly one ConversationTurn on the observer session through the normal queue entry point, carrying a structured payload.

idempotency.why: conversation_turn has UNIQUE (session_id, client_turn_id), so a redelivered match collapses onto the turn already enqueued instead of waking the session twice. This is the same mechanism TASK_RUN_TRIGGER already uses for sched:/dep:/first-run:/batch: turns.
idempotency.heldByAnotherTurn: clientTurnId is the caller's own choice on every door into createTurn, so a turn somebody else queued can already hold a wake's key. Only a turn with the wake's exact payload collapses a redelivery. A turn with another payload is not the wake, the wake cannot be queued under the key it holds, and the delivery becomes a DEAD_LETTER at once (WAKE_KEY_TAKEN) — unless the observer's life is over, which is refused as such (OBSERVER_SESSION_*).
idempotency.recognizedKeys: A drain, an interrupt or a withdrawal (states.delivery) takes a queued turn for a wake only under a key the worker writes: watch:<watchId>:<generation> with the generation in canonical decimal (no leading zero, within integer range), or watch:<watchId>:expired, :revoked or :unresolvable, each for its own end's delivery kind. A turn under any other watch: key is an ordinary message, and taking it off the queue changes no delivery.

sendIntent.why: A wake is new work, never a steer into the turn already running. CURRENT_WORK would be refused as CURRENT_WORK_UNAVAILABLE whenever no live in-flight message exists, which is precisely the common case for a parked observer.

actions.runningObserver: No special case: an observer that is RUNNING keeps its status and the turn queues behind the running one (statusAfterTurnEnqueued leaves RUNNING alone and moves AWAITING_INPUT/INTERRUPTED to PENDING). Watch never resumes a session concurrently because it never bypasses the queue.
actions.forbidden: Polling logs or shell transcript text must never be put into the payload.

endTurns.why: A session waiting on a watch is told when the watch ends unmatched, or it waits forever (§3, §5). A watch reaches one terminal state, so it owes at most one such turn, and each end's key ends in a word no generation number spells.

REVOKED.note: §7: the turn names the end and nothing about the targets, their state or any snapshot.

UNRESOLVABLE.note: Every target is GONE, so nothing about them is left to report.

notDelivered.CANCELLED: The owner or the observer cancelled the watch, so nobody waiting on it is left uninformed.

endTurns.notifyUser: A NOTIFY_USER watch has no waiting session, so none of these ends is delivered for it.

refusals.when: The snapshot resolved to zero targets; ALL over an empty set would be vacuously true.
A leaf's targetKind does not match a target's kind.
Nesting exceeds limits.maxPredicateDepth or operands exceed maxOperandsPerComposite.
A kind outside aggregations/composites, or a leaf outside leaves.
The request's predicateVersion is not served by this build.
A TASK_LIST/PROJECT ref was given as live membership rather than a creation-time snapshot source.
A RESUME_SESSION watch names its own observer session among its targets.
A RESUME_SESSION watch names a session its own observer already wakes, directly or through a chain of live (ACTIVE or PAUSED) RESUME_SESSION watches: the new watch would close a wake cycle.

A watch that stays live after its first evaluation would give the account more than limits.maxLiveWatchesPerOwner live watches, or one of its targets more than limits.maxLiveWatchesPerTarget. A watch matched at create occupies no live slot and is not refused.
The observer cannot read every target at create time.

deliveryGuards.why: A Match is recorded once, but what it causes costs a turn or reaches a device, and a stored snapshot can outlive the permission that let it be taken. So every attempt is checked again when it is made, and every wake counts against what one session and one account may be given.
deliveryGuards.permissionRecheck: Before any payload is built, every target of the watch that still exists must belong to the watch's owner, and so must the observer session. Otherwise the delivery is a PERMISSION_REVOKED dead letter and nothing about the targets leaves the database. The watch keeps its state: a Match is immutable and every watch end is terminal. A REVOKED or UNRESOLVABLE end's turn carries no target, so only its observer is rechecked.
deliveryGuards.redaction: A wake's payload is rebuilt from the stored snapshot through an allowlist: each target's kind, id, epoch, state and changed; the leaves the grammar declares, answered true or false; observed status, endReason, runState, lifecycleState and pendingApproval, each a single word or a boolean. Any other key is dropped, a value of the wrong shape is written [redacted], and so is a reason outside the predicate vocabulary. A lastError has URL credentials, bearer tokens, API keys and key=value secrets replaced by [redacted] before it is stored.
deliveryGuards.continuousSpacing: A CONTINUOUS watch's Match deliveries are at least limits.continuousDebounceSeconds apart. One due sooner goes back to PENDING until then, its lastError headed CONTINUOUS_RATE_LIMITED, and no attempt is counted.
deliveryGuards.storm: A RESUME_SESSION wake whose observer session was already given limits.maxWakesPerObserverPerHour wakes in the last hour is a WAKE_STORM_SUPPRESSED dead letter. Counted under the observer's row lock, so the limit is exact.
deliveryGuards.budget: A RESUME_SESSION wake whose owner's watches already gave limits.maxWakesPerOwnerPerDay wakes in the last 24 hours is a WAKE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED dead letter. Wakes to different observers of one account do not wait on each other, so concurrent ones may pass the budget by as many as are in flight.
deliveryGuards.counted: A wake counts while its delivery is DELIVERED. One its observer's queue lost unrun is a dead letter and no longer counts.

OBSERVER_SESSION_GONE.when: The observer session does not exist, or the watch names none.

OBSERVER_SESSION_IN_TRASH.when: The observer session is in Trash, and a watch does not restore it.

OBSERVER_SESSION_COMPLETED.when: The observer session was moved to Completed, and a watch does not reopen it.

OBSERVER_SESSION_ENDED.when: The observer's run was over, or it ended while the wake was still queued (section 3).

OBSERVER_SESSION_UNAVAILABLE.when: The queue entry point refused the observer session for any other reason.

OBSERVER_TURN_INTERRUPTED.when: An interrupt deleted the queued wake (section 3).

WAKE_WITHDRAWN.when: The owner withdrew the queued wake (section 3).

TURN_REFUSED.when: The queue entry point refused the turn.

LEASE_EXPIRED.when: Workers holding the delivery kept stopping before they settled it, until its attempts ran out.

ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED.when: Retryable failures reached limits.maxDeliveryAttempts. It heads no lastError, whose text is the last failure.

OTHER.when: Any dead letter this build does not classify.

redrive.effect: The dead letter goes back to PENDING, due at once, with its attempts counted from zero, and the worker attempts it again under every guard above. Its lastError stays until the next attempt writes one.

refused.DELIVERY_NOT_DEAD_LETTER: Only a dead letter is redriven.
refused.DELIVERY_NOT_RETRYABLE: Its code is retryable: false. A wake that left its observer's queue unrun is not queued a second time, and a payload whose permission was revoked is not delivered.

factSource.authoritative: PostgreSQL rows named by each leaf's sourceColumns, read inside the evaluating transaction.

accelerantOnly.durability: never persisted; at-most-once; no ack, no retry
accelerantOnly.ordering: not guaranteed per connection (streamForUser uses mergeMap over an async mapper)
accelerantOnly.replay: none: no cursor and no Last-Event-ID on the control plane
accelerantOnly.onRestart: everything in flight is lost; the hub is process memory
namedDropPaths: pg_notify failure is caught and warn-logged only
payload over MAX_NOTIFY_BYTES degrades to a seq-signal, and synthetic control events carry seq 0 with no persisted row to re-read
owner or session summary resolves null mid-flight

accelerantOnly.coalescing: repeated signals collapse into one unconsumed row with an occurrences counter, so a consumer may not assume one row per occurrence

coverageGap.consequence: session.completed_at is NOT in that column list, so moving a Session to Completed writes no outbox row at all, and Approval writes are on a different table entirely. SESSION_LIFECYCLE_TERMINAL and SESSION_NEEDS_ATTENTION therefore have leaves no durable event covers: the sweep is load-bearing for them, not a backstop.

factSource.invariant: Dropping every hint changes only latency. Liveness is owned by nextEvaluateAt plus the leased reconciliation sweep.
factSource.forbidden: A Match must never be derived from the content of an event payload.

agentSurface.why: An agent that has to wait on Orbit's own work (tasks reaching a status, sessions finishing a turn) asks the server to watch it and ends its turn, instead of holding the turn open in a sleep loop or a background process that dies with its engine.

runnerDoor.observer: The calling session named by X-Orbit-Session-Id, which must be a session this runner hosts. It observes every watch this door creates; a body cannot name another, and every read and edit is confined to the watches that session observes.
runnerDoor.action: RESUME_SESSION unless the request names NOTIFY_USER.
runnerDoor.sessionTargets: A watch that names a SESSION target also needs the calling session's orchestration credential, the authority session_get needs. A watch over TASK targets needs none, as task_get needs none.
runnerDoor.headless: Refused: outside a session there is nothing to wake.

release.why: A caller that got its answer inline takes back what the watch still owes its session, so the answer arrives once: inline, or as the wake, never both.

outcomes.CANCELLED: The watch was still ACTIVE or PAUSED. It is cancelled, and a cancelled watch wakes nobody.
outcomes.WAKE_WITHDRAWN: The watch had ended and its wake turn was queued. The turn is withdrawn and its delivery becomes a DEAD_LETTER under WAKE_WITHDRAWN, as an owner's withdrawal does (section 3).
outcomes.WAKE_NOT_QUEUED: The watch ended but its wake is not queued yet (the delivery is PENDING or IN_FLIGHT), or it is still settling. Ask again shortly.
outcomes.ALREADY_WOKEN: A runner already took the wake turn, so nothing is left to withdraw.
outcomes.NOTHING_OWED: Nothing will wake the session for this watch: it was cancelled, it notifies the user instead, or its delivery is already a dead letter.

sessionCreateWait.order: The watch is recorded before the wait begins, so a caller killed or cut off mid-wait leaves it behind to wake its session.
sessionCreateWait.inline: A session that settles within the wait budget is returned in full, exactly as before, and the call releases the watch.

handedBack.TIMEOUT: The wait budget ran out. The call returns the session as last seen with the watch beside it, still waiting.
handedBack.TRANSPORT_ERROR: The control plane stopped answering mid-wait. The call returns the session as last seen with the watch beside it instead of an error.

sessionCreateWait.legacy: No calling session (a headless CLI), or a control plane without the runner door: the poll that predates watches, unchanged.

vectors.why: AWAITING_INPUT left PENDING/RUNNING, so the turn settled, but the session is alive and still Open.
The headline separation: an agent parking for input is not a completion criterion being satisfied.
A bare INTERRUPTED is a stopped turn on a live, schedulable session.
Any recorded endReason means the session itself ended, settling ENDED.
Succeeded-and-Open is a normal state; run outcome and list membership are orthogonal.
DONE is the projection of a satisfied criterion, not of a session finishing.
Terminal is the union DONE/CANCELLED/FAILED; failure is the narrower question.
The canonical agent request: wake me when all seven settle or any one fails. The ANY branch fires first.
ALL over nothing is vacuously true and would fire instantly; it is refused at create instead.
A task leaf cannot be evaluated against a session row.
Creation evaluates once; a satisfied condition produces a Match rather than waiting for a future change.
One-shot settles at MATCHED; the unique index makes a duplicate impossible rather than unlikely.
Hints only schedule evaluation; the row state decides, so replays and reordering are absorbed.
A session blocked on an approval is asking a human something while its turn is still unsettled; needs-attention and settled are independent axes.
The 0133 session trigger fires only on status/deleted_at/merge_status, so moving a session to Completed writes no durable event; a watch that trusted the event stream would wait forever.
Correctness may not depend on the event stream; the sweep is what makes a lost NOTIFY a latency bug only.
A GONE target leaves the set and is recorded; it is never silently counted as satisfied.
A watch that can never be decided must say so; stopping quietly is the failure mode being designed out.
Permission is rechecked where the payload is built, so a revocation after the Match cannot leak target state. The Match stays the fact it was, and its delivery says why nothing was delivered.
A session waiting on a watch that expires must be told, or it waits forever.
Delivery goes through the normal queue, so a running session is never concurrently resumed.
A session that wakes itself is an unbounded wake loop.
A Match is an immutable fact about the epoch it observed; later reopening does not rewrite history.
Debounce and coalescing are what keep a continuous watch from becoming a wake storm.
v1 freezes the target set at create; live membership needs sealed semantics that do not exist yet.
A revoked watch may not tell anyone what it can no longer read, and it may not leave the session waiting on it waiting forever either.
A watch that can never be decided has to say so to the session waiting on it, not only to whoever reads the watch.
The owner or the observer cancelled the watch, so nobody waiting on it is left uninformed.

given.request: a watch whose condition does not hold yet

vectors.why: Every live watch is evaluated again every reconciliation period, so an account cannot make that cost unbounded. A refused create writes nothing.
S2 settling wakes S1, and S1's turn settling would wake S2: two sessions waking each other are the self-watch loop with one more hop.
A session woken that often is almost certainly looping. The next wake stops at a dead letter anyone can see, not another turn.
Every wake is a turn somebody pays for. Past the budget a wake waits where its owner can see it and redrive it.
A continuous watch cannot wake its observer faster than its window, however fast its generations are recorded.
A wake that left its observer's queue unrun was taken back on purpose; redriving it would wake a session its owner stopped.
